title: Minuta 2025-12-18
summary: The minutes of the 18 December decision (a fifth consecutive 25bp cut, to 7.00%, again split 4-1 with Heath dissenting for a hold at 7.25%) keep the board easing but read modestly LESS dovish than the 6 November minutes. The forward guidance was softened again: the board dropped 'valorara recortar la tasa de referencia' and now says only that it 'valorara el momento de realizar ajustes adicionales' -- 'adjustments', not cuts, with the emphasis on timing -- while the dominant majority theme is explicitly one of 'mayor gradualidad y cautela' and a transition toward 'niveles de tasas mas convencionales', with several members stressing the cycle should slow in H1 2026 and one favoring a 'wait and see' approach. The dovish pillars are intact and, if anything, broader: activity stayed weak (Q3 GDP -0.29%, ~0.3% growth for 2025, the output gap widening in negative territory), investment and the labor market keep cooling with wages moderating, and the peso reached its most appreciated level of 2025 while the Fed's third consecutive cut gives room without compressing the differential. The counterweight sharpened: core inflation rose to a year-high 4.54% in the second half of November, non-housing/education services stay above 5%, the inflation balance of risks is still tilted up (though 'considerablemente menos pronunciado que el de 2021 a 2024'), and members now note the stance sits near the midpoint of the neutral range with the 2026 IEPS and tariff increases adding one-off upside. Net, the board is still cutting with the cycle 'not concluded', but the softer 'adjustments' guidance and the pervasive gradualism-and-caution language tilt it a notch back from the November minutes.

key_quotes.quote: la Junta de Gobierno, con la presencia de todos sus miembros, decidió por mayoría reducir en 25 puntos base el objetivo para la Tasa de Interés Interbancaria a un día a un nivel de 7.00%.
key_quotes.context: Collegial decision: fifth straight 25bp cut, to 7.00%, by majority with one dissent (Heath, hold at 7.25%)

key_quotes.quote: Hacia delante, la Junta de Gobierno valorará el momento de realizar ajustes adicionales a la tasa de referencia.
key_quotes.context: Softened forward guidance: 'will assess the timing of additional ADJUSTMENTS', dropping the November 'valorara recortar la tasa de referencia' and no longer naming cuts

key_quotes.quote: Uno señaló que el balance de riesgos para la inflación en el horizonte de pronóstico mantiene un sesgo al alza, si bien considerablemente menos pronunciado que el de 2021 a 2024.
key_quotes.context: Inflation balance of risks still tilted up, though judged much less pronounced than in 2021-2024; core hit a year-high 4.54% in late November

key_quotes.quote: Argumentó que, si en esta ocasión se decide disminuir la tasa de referencia en 25 puntos base, la postura monetaria se situaría aún más cerca del punto medio del rango estimado para la tasa neutral.
key_quotes.context: Heath (dissent): a further cut would put the stance even closer to the midpoint of the estimated neutral range, i.e. limited remaining room
